title: Divine Mercy: The Revelations to St. Faustina Kowalska
summary: In the 1930s, Jesus Christ appeared repeatedly to St. Maria Faustina Kowalska, entrusting her with a renewed proclamation of God's merciful love. The devotion centers on trust in Christ, conversion, the Divine Mercy image, the Chaplet, the Hour of Mercy, and Divine Mercy Sunday.

blocks.text: 1. St. Faustina and Her Historical Setting

St. Maria Faustina Kowalska (1905–1938) was a Polish sister of the Congregation of Our Lady of Mercy. Serving in simple roles such as cook and porter, she developed a deep mystical life recorded in her Diary under the guidance of her confessor, Blessed Michał Sopoćko.
2. The Principal Revelations

On February 22, 1931, in Płock, Faustina experienced a vision of Jesus clothed in white with pale and red rays streaming from his Heart, symbolizing the water of Baptism/Holy Spirit and the blood of the Eucharist.

blocks.title: Words of Christ to St. Faustina (Diary 47)
blocks.text: “Paint an image according to the pattern you see, with the signature: 'Jesus, I trust in You.' I desire that this image be venerated, first in your chapel, and then throughout the world.”
The revelations introduced core devotional practices: the Divine Mercy Image, the Chaplet prayed on Rosary beads, the Hour of Mercy (3:00 PM), and the Novena leading to Divine Mercy Sunday.

Jesus came and stood among them and said to them, 'Peace be with you.' ... 'Receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them; if you withhold forgiveness from any, it is withheld.'
Exegesis: Divine Mercy originates in the Paschal Mystery. The risen Christ communicates his victory over sin by giving peace and instituting the sacramental ministry of forgiveness in the Church.
3. The Core Message

The devotion asserts that God is rich in mercy and calls sinners to approach him with complete trust. This trust is not passive optimism but a call to active conversion, sacramental reception, and living out corporal and spiritual works of mercy.

blocks.title: The Spiritual Center
blocks.text: Divine Mercy is the Gospel proclamation that Christ's merciful love seeks out sinners, invites them to repentance, and transforms them into instruments of mercy toward others.
4. Public vs. Private Revelation

Public Revelation ended with the Apostles. The writings of St. Faustina constitute private revelation; they highlight the Gospel's eternal message of mercy using devotional language suited to the modern world without adding new dogma.

blocks.title: CCC 67: Private Revelation
blocks.text: Private revelations do not belong to the deposit of faith. Their role is to help believers live Christ's definitive revelation more fully in a specific historical context.
5. Investigation and Church Approval

Due to faulty translations, the Holy Office issued a restriction on the devotion in 1959. After extensive re-examination of original manuscripts, the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith lifted all prohibitions in 1978.
Pope John Paul II beatified Sister Faustina in 1993 and canonized her on April 30, 2000, simultaneously establishing Divine Mercy Sunday for the universal Church on the Second Sunday of Easter.

blocks.title: Church Approval Status
blocks.text: Following early restrictions, the devotion received full ecclesial vindication in 1978. St. Faustina was canonized in 2000, and Divine Mercy Sunday was added to the universal Roman Calendar.
Blessed are the merciful, for they shall receive mercy.
Exegesis: Receiving divine forgiveness requires a heart open to extending mercy to others through forgiveness, charity, and active care for those in need.
6. Pastoral Application

Authentic practice pairs devotion—such as the Chaplet or 3:00 PM prayer—with sacramental confession, Eucharistic adoration, and active works of charity, placing full confidence in Christ's forgiving love.

blocks.title: Central Lesson
blocks.text: Divine Mercy reflects the heart of the Gospel: Christ meets us in our weakness, grants forgiveness through his sacraments, and commands us to show mercy to our neighbor.

blocks.title: Closing Prayer
blocks.text: O merciful Jesus, deepen our faith in your Paschal Mystery and teach us to trust your love. Forgive our sins, heal our wounds, and give us the grace to approach your mercy with sincere repentance. Make us merciful toward our neighbors in thought, word, and deed. Through the intercession of St. Maria Faustina Kowalska, may we proclaim: Jesus, I trust in You. Amen.
